cards.text: Ezekiel the prophet has already brought God's word against Pharaoh and all Egypt (Ezekiel 29:2), and now the word of the LORD comes to him again. God tells him to declare: "Wail, 'Alas for that day!'" When a message opens with WAIL, friend, that is not a birthday card.

cards.question: Ezekiel's message says that day is near. Which day is it?
True or false: God says this coming day will be a time of peace for the nations.

cards.text: Then it gets specific: God says a sword will come against Egypt. The slain will fall, its wealth will be taken away, and its foundations will be torn down.

cards.question: When the slain fall in Egypt, there will be ___ in Cush, Egypt's neighbor to the south.

cards.text: And Egypt won't fall alone. Cush, Put, Lud, Libya, all the various peoples and the men of the covenant land will fall with her by the sword.

cards.question: Egypt's allies will fall, and God says her proud strength will ___.

cards.text: They will fall by the sword within her, from Migdol to Syene. They'll be desolate among desolate lands, and their cities will lie among ruined cities.

cards.question: God says He will set fire to Egypt, and all her helpers will be shattered. When that happens, what will they know?

cards.text: On that day, God says, messengers will go out from Him in ships. Their destination: Cush.

cards.question: Why do God's messengers sail out to Cush?

answers.text: To frighten Cush out of complacency
To call Cush to come help Egypt
To carry off the wealth of Cush

cards.text: Frightened out of complacency, like dozing on the couch when your boss texts "Got a minute?" and suddenly you are WIDE awake. Anguish will come upon them on the day of Egypt's doom, and God says, "For it is indeed coming."
Then God names who will do it. He says, "I will put an end to the hordes of Egypt by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon."

cards.question: True or false: God calls Nebuchadnezzar and his people the most ruthless of the nations.

cards.text: Nebuchadnezzar and his people will be brought in to destroy the land. They will draw their swords against Egypt and fill the land with the slain.

cards.question: God isn't done with Egypt's land yet. What does He say He'll do to its streams?
God says He'll sell the land to the wicked and bring desolation on it by the hands of ___.

cards.text: Then God closes it out: "I, the LORD, have spoken."
The Lord GOD keeps going, and now He starts naming places in Egypt, beginning with Memphis. He says He will destroy the idols and put an end to the images there.

cards.question: True or false: God says Egypt will still have a prince.
God says He will instill ___ in the land of Egypt.

cards.text: Then comes a roll call of places across Egypt: Pathros, Zoan, Thebes, Pelusium, On and Pi-beseth. Fire, wrath, the sword and captivity, and not ONE of them gets good news.
Then Tahpanhes, another city in Egypt. The day will be darkened there when God breaks the yoke of Egypt.

cards.question: When Egypt's proud strength comes to an end, a ___ will cover her.

cards.text: Egypt's daughters will go into captivity. God sums it all up: He will execute judgment on Egypt, and they will know that He is the LORD.
Now a new date: the eleventh year, on the seventh day of the first month. The word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel again, and this time it's about Pharaoh king of Egypt.

cards.question: God tells Ezekiel He has broken something of Pharaoh's, and it hasn't been bound up for healing or splinted. What is it?

cards.text: Not bound up, not splinted, like going to urgent care and walking out with a PAMPHLET. Then God says, "Behold, I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt."

cards.question: God isn't done with Pharaoh's broken arm. What does He say He'll break?

answers.text: The strong arm and the broken one

cards.question: God says He will make the ___ fall from Pharaoh's hand.

cards.text: On top of that, God says He will disperse the Egyptians among the nations and scatter them throughout the lands.

cards.question: True or false: God says He will strengthen the arms of Babylon's king.
True or false: God says Pharaoh will groan before Babylon's king like a mortally wounded man.

cards.text: God says Pharaoh's arms will fall limp, and He will place His own sword in the hand of Babylon's king to wield against the land of Egypt. Then that scattering line comes back, and they will know that He is the LORD.
